WV-2026-HB5692.title: Supplemental appropriation, State Road Fund
WV-2026-HB5692.aiSummary: The bill adds $100 million from the State Road Fund to the West Virginia Division of Highways for other federal aid programs in fiscal year 2026. It would increase money for the Department of Transportation for the year ending June 30, 2026. The bill became law.

WV-2026-HB5689.title: Supplemental appropriation, Department of Homeland Security
WV-2026-HB5689.aiSummary: The bill would add state money from a surplus fund to the Department of Homeland Security for fiscal year 2026. It would increase funding for Information Technology Services by $6,642,874 and Special Services by $5,002,392 for correctional units.

WV-2026-HB5353.title: To bring virtual currency kiosks within the purview of money transmission licensure and create disclosure requirements and daily transaction limitations for new and existing customers.

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 655)

WV-2026-HB5353.aiSummary: The bill would treat virtual currency kiosks, like machines that exchange cash for virtual currency, as money transmitters that need a state license. It would also require them to give disclosures and set daily limits on transactions for new and existing customers. The bill was approved by the governor and became law in 2026.

WV-2026-HB4798.title: Permitting teachers to wear a “mobile alert button” for emergency situations, to be known as “Alyssa’s Law.”

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 380)

WV-2026-HB4798.aiSummary: The law lets schools use wearable panic alert devices, or mobile alert buttons, in public schools if funding is available. These devices must connect with 911 and help trigger a schoolwide lockdown notice, and school staff who use them must be trained each year. It also creates a state fund for this equipment and related school safety gear, and the law ends on December 31, 2029.

WV-2026-HB4390.aiSummary: The law gives some kinship parents a temporary payment equal to a foster parent subsidy when a child is first placed with them, if they pass a background check, the home check, and are assigned help to work toward foster parent certification. The higher payment starts within 30 days of placement and can last for up to six months. It became law in 2026.

WV-2026-HB4354.aiSummary: The law sets rules for clothing and other needed items for children who are removed from home and placed in foster, kinship, or residential care. It requires a review at placement, and it sets a minimum initial clothing allowance of $375. It also lays out how the money may be paid, including a reloadable payment card, a purchasing card, or reimbursement to the caregiver.

WV-2026-HB4138.aiSummary: The law expands who must register as a sex offender, including people convicted of certain sex crimes and some other crimes found to be sexually motivated. It also requires more personal details at registration, such as address, employer, vehicles, internet names, phone numbers, and some ID records. People who must register must pay a $125 annual fee, and the money goes to the State Police.

WV-2026-HB5638.title: Relating to the requirements of the state’s cyber security program and responsibilities and authority of the state chief information security officer

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 644)
To House Energy and Public Works

WV-2026-HB5638.aiSummary: This law changes the state cybersecurity program and expands the duties of the state chief information security officer. It creates a West Virginia Cybersecurity Office, sets rules and standards for state agencies, and requires agencies to do cyber risk reviews and follow security policies. It also lets the office charge some exempt public bodies for voluntary help and protects certain cybersecurity records from public release.

WV-2026-HB5515.title: Relating to modernizing and updating workers’ compensation statutes.

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and and title amendmentpassed bill (Roll No. 647)
Passed Senate with amended title (Roll No. 571)
Reported do pass, with amendment and title amendment

WV-2026-HB5515.aiSummary: The law updates West Virginia workers’ compensation rules for reporting injuries and paying claims. It requires workers and employers to report injuries faster, and it sets steps for paying temporary disability and medical benefits while a claim is being reviewed. It also says benefits are paid directly to the claimant and gives rules for when overpaid amounts can be recovered.

WV-2026-HB5065.title: Relating to hotel occupancy tax.

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 682)
Passed Senate with amended title (Roll No. 555)
Reported do pass, with amendment and title amendment

WV-2026-HB5065.aiSummary: The law changes how hotel occupancy taxes are collected in cities and counties. It says the guest pays the tax, and hotels and online booking services must collect and send it to the right local tax office. It also sets rules for online booking services that handle enough West Virginia sales or transactions, including record keeping and how to send the money.

WV-2026-HB4996.title: Relating to bail in cases involving terroristic threats to schools or children

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 681)
Passed Senate with amended title (Roll No. 553)
Reported do pass, with amendment and title amendment

WV-2026-HB4996.aiSummary: This law changes rules for false emergency reports and threats of violent crime. It makes some threats to commit violence a felony and lets courts bar certain people on release from living or working within 1,000 feet of the threatened place or person. It also lets courts order repayment of emergency response costs, and it does not apply to an authorized emergency drill.

WV-2026-HB4990.title: Relating to crimes using gift cards

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 680)
Passed Senate with amended title (Roll No. 408)
Reported do pass, with amendment and title amendment

WV-2026-HB4990.aiSummary: The bill creates crimes for stealing, tampering with, or tricking someone to get gift cards or gift card access info. It sets different penalties based on value, with misdemeanor charges under $1,000 and felony charges over $1,000. The law applies to people who act with intent to defraud and became Chapter 105 in 2026.

WV-2026-HB4819.title: Relating to use of criminal records as disqualification from authorization to practice a particular profession
WV-2026-HB4819.aiSummary: The law changes how criminal records can be used when deciding whether someone may get a license or other approval to work in a profession. If a criminal background check is used, it must include the outcome of any arrest or charge. It applies to people seeking approval to practice certain jobs in West Virginia, and it became law in 2026.

WV-2026-HB4765.title: Teacher, School Personnel, and State Police Pay Raise

actions.text: House refused to concur; requested Senate to recede (Voice)

Amendments to committee amendment adopted (Voice vote)
Committee amendment as amended adopted (Voice vote)

WV-2026-HB4765.aiSummary: The law changes pay rules for West Virginia State Police members and certain forensic lab staff. It sets new base pay starting July 1, 2026, with pay ranging from $52,644 for cadets in training to $90,102 for forensic scientist supervisor IV, and it adds service-step raises and up to $200 in extra pay per pay period for some state police members. It also starts a new market pay add-on based on local income data on December 1, 2026, with payments beginning July 1, 2027, and limited to 20% of base pay.

WV-2026-HB4552.title: Relating to the law-enforcement powers of correctional officers

actions.text: House concurred in Senate amendment and passed bill (Roll No. 691)

WV-2026-HB4552.aiSummary: The law changes the powers of some Division of Corrections and Rehabilitation officers. It lets certain correctional officers make arrests in set cases, investigate some crimes in correctional facilities, and be approved to carry firearms on duty if they finish required training. It also keeps a special response team and sets rules for concealed carry, firearms training, and related ID cards for qualifying officers.
